idiom_name: trait mixins with abstract members plus higher-order functions; Resource/Ref for effectful state
implementation_notes: Scala composes reusable behaviour through traits: the tour documents mixin composition where a trait implements behaviour over abstract members (RichIterator over AbsIterator) and a class combines one superclass with many traits, which replaces wrapper and inheritance hierarchies because behaviour can be stacked without diamond rules. In function form the same idea is a method returning a state/actions pair built from higher-order functions and lazy vals; for effectful state the ecosystem equivalents are scoped resource types and mutable references composed with flatMap/for-comprehensions (cats-effect Resource/Ref, ZIO ZLayer) - that last point is analysis of those libraries rather than a quoted claim. Prefer a plain class or a trait with a self-type when behaviour is shared across unrelated hosts, and keep the functional-resource form when the unit owns acquisition and release.
pitfalls: Traits with mutable state are mixed into every host instance; sharing one behaviour object between hosts needs an explicit instance or a singleton object.
Trait linearization is right-to-left, so which override wins depends on mixin order; self-type mismatches fail at compile time, but conflicting concrete members can still surprise.
Implicit/given parameters make a unit's dependencies invisible at the call site; expose them explicitly once the behaviour crosses module boundaries.
